Discipline of citation. Every value below cites EvidenceItem nodes whose sources[] resolves to real graph node IDs (SYS-*, STORE-*, FLOW-*, STK-*, ROLE-*, ACT-*, GDPR-C*, CRA-C*, NIST-*) — empty or unresolvable sources fail scripts/build_p1_dashboard.py --check Gate 3. This Folio does NOT assign Tiers. Per MATURITY_MODEL_CSF_STRICT.md §4 Tier decisions require the §4 escada rule applied to evidence for all characteristic questions of each Tier — a P7 activity. What this Folio shows is the evidence available for that decision.

How evidence works discipline of citation

Each EvidenceItem node in the graph holds:

  • subdomain_id — ONE AEGIS sub-domain (D-XX.Y)
  • scale — coverage (Scale B) or capability (Scale A)
  • outcome — a regulatory clause id (Coverage) or a CSF/PF subcategory (Capability)
  • claim — one-sentence observable fact; never a Tier number
  • sources[] — ≥1 graph node IDs. empty ⇒ Gate 3 FAIL
  • observed — true (present) or false (declared gap)

The two radars above visualise Scale A across both overlays. The tier-bar shows the same data as a horizontal segment strip. The Coverage table (below) shows Scale B, anchored on GDPR/CRA clauses — and now also lists the PF anchor from OVERLAY_NIST_PF_1.1.md §2.

Scale B — Coverage per sub-domain

One EvidenceItem per active sub-domain, citing a regulatory clause and verifiable graph-node sources. observed=False flags gaps. PF anchor column shows the matching PF subcategory per OVERLAY_NIST_PF_1.1.md §2.

Scale A — Capability by CSF 2.0 Function

EvidenceItems anchored on CSF 2.0 subcategories per OVERLAY_NIST_CSF_2.0.md §2. Tier assignment deferred to P7.
